To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
reverse-phase protein microarrays are a useful and powerful tool to identify HER2 signaling activation even in the absence of HER2 overexpression.
Reverse-phase protein microarray analysis highlights HER2 signaling pathway activation in IHC/FISH-negative breast tumors.

HER2 signaling activation, as detected by reverse-phase protein array, was independent from total expression of HER2 and involved HER3 activation in a subset of IHC/Fisher/HER2- breast cancers, which could potentially benefit from anti-HER2 targeted therapy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and validation of novel molecular diagnostic and prognostic tests based on the use of reverse-phase microarray technology.
the development and application of novel molecular tools and technologies for the comprehensive analysis of the molecular mechanisms underlying cancer development.
the development of a novel, high throughput, multiplex and quantitative protein analysis platform based on reverse-phase microarray technology.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this research is a significant step forward toward the development of a personalized therapy approach for patients affected by breast cancer.
reverse-phase protein microarrays are able to identify a subgroup of HER2- patients with activated HER2 signaling, thus opening the way to a more personalized treatment of breast cancer.
reverse-phase protein microarrays are a powerful tool for the identification of molecular targets for novel therapies and the selection of patients for targeted therapies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HER2 signaling activation, independent of total HER2 expression, can occur in HER2- breast tumors.
HER2 signaling activation is not limited to HER2+ tumors, and it can be detected in HER2- tumors by reverse-phase protein analysis.
reverse-phase protein microarrays are an important tool to identify novel targets for the treatment of HER2-negative breast cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we were able to demonstrate that there are patients who have HER2 signaling activation but do not express HER2.

reverse-phase protein microarrays are a powerful tool to perform a detailed molecular characterization of HER2 signaling and its partners in breast cancer and could be useful to identify patients who would benefit from HER2-targeted therapy.
we have identified a subset of HER2-negative patients that have high HER2 signaling and may benefit from targeted therapies.
